---
title: "Ohm's law and power"
subtitle: "Electrical engineering basics"
toc: true
---

The relationship every other circuit identity gets built on top of.

## The law

For a resistor, voltage and current are proportional:

$$
V = IR
$$

Power dissipated follows from $P = VI$, substituted with Ohm's law to give two more useful forms:

$$
P = VI = I^2 R = \frac{V^2}{R}
$$

The $I^2R$ form is the one that matters for sizing: double the current through a fixed resistance and dissipation quadruples, not doubles — a common reason parts run hotter than expected after a "small" current increase.

## Calculator

Enter a supply voltage and resistance to get current and dissipated power.

```{=html}
<div id="ohms-calc"></div>
<script>
Calc.create({
  root: "ohms-calc",
  inputs: [
    { id: "V", label: "Voltage V (V)", value: 5, min: 0, step: 0.1 },
    { id: "R", label: "Resistance R (Ω)", value: 220, min: 0.01, step: 1 }
  ],
  outputs: [
    { id: "I", label: "Current I" },
    { id: "P", label: "Power P" }
  ],
  compute: function (v) {
    if (v.R <= 0) return { I: "-", P: "-" };
    var I = v.V / v.R;
    var P = v.V * I;
    var Itxt = Math.abs(I) < 1 ? (I * 1000).toFixed(2) + " mA" : I.toFixed(3) + " A";
    var Ptxt = Math.abs(P) < 1 ? (P * 1000).toFixed(2) + " mW" : P.toFixed(3) + " W";
    return { I: Itxt, P: Ptxt };
  }
});
</script>
```
